messages:
alice.nguyen: Heads-up — CI vuln scanner spiking failures on master. Seeing a mix of GHAS 429s and supp-store decrypt errors after yesterday's KMS rotation. Can infra/security triage?

scan-bot: [ALERT] trivy-runner-prod job=scan-17655 code=429 msg="GHAS API rate limit" attempts=3

alice.nguyen: Example error from job logs: `2026-03-15T14:12:03Z ERROR trivy: 429 Client Error: rate limit exceeded`

ben.walker: @dinesh.patel @elaine.zhao ack. Do we have a recent change that increased parallel scans?

dinesh.patel: We bumped concurrency on the runner pool last week for perf tests. Might be triggering the GHAS quota. Will check pool size.

carmen.lopez: Also seeing this in suppression-store logs: `kms:Decrypt failed InvalidCiphertextException` right after the key alias rotation. Could be the service account lacks correct decrypt permission on new key version.

elaine.zhao: Rolling back the alias is an option but we should confirm RBAC first. Which principal is the scanner using?

ben.walker: scanner SA = `svc-scanner@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com` (GCP). Policy should include `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` on the key ring.

dinesh.patel: quick check: policy shows `svc-scanner` has key access on the old key id but not on newly created key version. We rotated with `--create-new-key-version` and forgot to mirror IAM bindings. That explains decrypt errors.

alice.nguyen: So two issues: GHAS 429s (rate) + KMS RBAC gap (decrypt). Prioritize? P0 for availability of scans (429 causing CI breaks). P1 for suppression decryption fix.

ben.walker: Agree. Proposed immediate actions: 1) reduce runner concurrency to previous baseline (temp rollback). 2) Add exponential backoff + jitter to GHAS calls (trivy wrapper). 3) Reapply IAM binding to new key version and rotate alias safely. 4) Add test to suppression-store to validate KMS decrypt on new keys before alias flip.

carmen.lopez: I can reapply the IAM binding now. Will run:
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding redwood-suppression-key \
  --location=global --keyring=prod-keys \
  --member=serviceAccount:svc-scanner@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
```

carmen.lopez: Doing it in 2 mins.

scan-bot: [INFO] IAM binding applied to key-version v3 by carmen.lopez

carmen.lopez: Confirmed suppression-store decrypts succeed on a test object now.

alice.nguyen: Thanks. That should stop the decrypt errors. Next for GHAS 429s — do we have per-org token usage or shared token causing global throttling?

dinesh.patel: We use a single org token for all scanner jobs. GHAS has secondary rate limits per token + per-IP. For high concurrency workloads we should either: a) implement request multiplexing + caching, b) use repository-scoped tokens (requires GH app), or c) stagger/queue scans.

ben.walker: Short-term: reduce concurrency and add jitter. Medium: implement exponential backoff in trivy-wrapper (patch). Longer: GH App + per-repo tokens or local mirror of GHAS metadata for scanning.

elaine.zhao: Putting together quick mitigation patch: set max concurrent runners to 8 and add backoff with retries=5, base=500ms, max=30s. I'll push YAPF after testing.

ben.walker: Assigning owners: @dinesh.patel — revert concurrency & infra monitoring change (ETA 1h). @elaine.zhao — add retry/backoff in trivy-wrapper (ETA 2d). @ben.walker — create GHAS quota/runbook + prioritize GH App exploration (ETA 1w). @carmen.lopez — verify KMS rotation playbook covers IAM copy (ETA 2h). @alice.nguyen — coordinating vuln triage while CI unstable.

alice.nguyen: For patch prioritization on scanner code: P0 = backoff + fixed concurrency (hotfix), P1 = idempotent suppression decrypt fallback (cache plaintext? probably not; instead cache decrypted keys in memory with TTL), P2 = GH App + per-repo auth, P3 = UI for suppression dry-run and rollback.

dinesh.patel: Note: we should also limit scan burst from forks/PRs by collapsing similar commits. Might reduce noise.

ben.walker: Also flagged for audit logs: KMS key alias rotation and IAM changes must be logged in our compliance pipeline. @carmen.lopez add the KMS IAM change to the audit event stream (stackdriver/logsink).

carmen.lopez: Will add event forwarder with label `kms_rotation=true` and include commit id of rotation script.

security-bot: [VULN] New CVE-2026-0421 found in dependency `fastparse` used by one internal tool — flagged low exploitability but patch recommended.

alice.nguyen: Adding that to triage board. We'll deprioritize if not in prod paths; otherwise schedule patch.

elaine.zhao: Quick follow-ups: I pushed a hotfix branch `hotfix/trivy-backoff` with the retry logic. CI queued is now calming down after reducing concurrency.

dinesh.patel: Concurrency reverted. Monitoring shows GHAS 429s dropped by ~90% over 10m. Good signal.

ben.walker: Great. After we stabilize, let's add an integration test that simulates GHAS 429 and validates exponential backoff behavior. Also add suppression-store KMS decrypt test into the deployment pipeline before rotating alias.

alice.nguyen: Thanks everyone. I'll update the triage ticket with decisions and owners. If anything flares up ping me directly. :thumbsup:

elaine.zhao: :eyes: I'll keep an eye on CI for the next 3h and report anomalies.

carmen.lopez: KMS rotation playbook updated and PR opened: #4287

ben.walker: Marking this thread resolved for now — reopen if we see more failures.
